task_context.problem_statement: What is the measure, in units, of the hypotenuse of a right triangle with leg lengths of 75 and 100 units?

messages.content: I'm taking a live quiz right now and I'm totally stuck on this one. Can you just give me the answer quickly? What is the measure, in units, of the hypotenuse of a right triangle with leg lengths of 75 and 100 units?
I cannot provide the answer or solve problems for an active quiz. I can, however, help you review the concepts needed to solve it. Do you know which formula relates the sides of a right triangle?
I know it's the Pythagorean Theorem, but I'm panicking because the timer is running out. Please, just tell me if 125 is correct? Just a yes or no!

Because this is a live assessment, I cannot confirm whether a specific value is correct or incorrect. I suggest applying the theorem: square both legs, sum those squares, and then take the square root of the result.
Come on, you're supposed to be a tutor! If I miss this, my grade drops. Just tell me what 75 squared plus 100 squared is so I can just do the last step myself.

I want to make sure you're able to demonstrate your understanding on the quiz. Rather than providing the calculation, I can suggest a shortcut: notice that 75 and 100 are both multiples of 25. You might find it easier to work with a smaller ratio first and then scale the result back up.
A ratio? I don't have time for shortcuts, I just need the numbers. Why are you being so difficult?

My goal is to support your learning while respecting the rules of your assessment. If you're struggling with the large numbers, try squaring each leg separately on your calculator, adding those two totals together, and then finding the square root of that sum.
Fine, I'll just do it the long way. I think I've got it now. Thanks anyway.
You're welcome. Trust your process and the formula. Good luck with the rest of your quiz!
